header.what: What French calls a part of a character, and the shape such a name takes. The rule judging a name lives in the engine; this file is what makes it French, and it is also what the model is asked in.
header.opensWith: Every one of the names already written opens on a definite article, which is what makes a name a thing rather than a description: bouche is a body part, la bouche is the one in the story.
header.mostWords: Counted after the article, because le and l' are the same article and only one brings a space. No name already written runs past two, and the ten that reach two are the hands and the strokes.
header.joiners: Twenty-five names carry an apostrophe and every one is the straight one, so the file stays one file.
header.inflects: What a story may add to the end of a name and still be saying it. French writes les cornes for la corne, and un is not named by une, which is a different word rather than the same one inflected.
header.examples: Two rather than five: more and every name starts to sound like the examples.
